text: however, large differences were seen on an individual level, leading the authors to conclude: 'as indicated by the wide limits of agreement . . . individual estimates of changes in body composition when taken alone should be interpreted with caution' (55). Similarly, a study that investigated agreement between 4C, 3C, and 2C models found all three methods gave acceptable group mean values, but on an individual level, only the 3C model served as a valid alternative to 4C (89).
